next_scope: Supplied-byte NTFS FILE_NAME and directory INDEX_ROOT/entry envelopes before source-bound namespace traversal.
rationale: The current FILE/attribute/list/stream and MFT bootstrap work does not interpret directory keys. Add bounded portable byte decoders with independent fixtures before following index children or exposing namespace claims.
observations: Microsoft documents a full parent reference and original UTF16 filename representation for NTFS3.0/3.1. Preserve raw names, namespace and original encoding separately from display and lookup; do not infer one name per file.

Pinned NTFS3 headers describe directory-entry keys, optional trailing child VBN and a distinct terminal entry. Index block sizing uses clusters when the block is at least one cluster and512-byte units otherwise. Do not reuse the signed boot size-code interpretation for the root byte.
proposed_boundary: Reuse portable/primitives checked views and existing NTFS3 profile controls; no native I/O, callbacks, mounting, lookup, collation, mutation, new frontend mode or public ABI.

Define entry/header/name bounds, terminal/child behavior, budget outcomes and raw identifier preservation before implementation/evaluation. Unknown/unsupported metadata must not manufacture a directory graph.
INDX fixups/index allocation and source-bound record/index acquisition need their own contracts and tests. No empty future source hierarchy or generic parsing framework.
open_details: Reconcile root block/count geometry and entry/header semantics against pinned sources before freezing private decoder expectations.
Choose concrete filename/index implementation ownership based on actual decoder consumers; update the existing source map and build/input registry when adding code.
Run independent guard/read-only/truncation/overflow/count/quota cases and actual C90/C++ header/dependency regressions. A private supplied-byte decoder does not qualify native namespace traversal.
